desc:
Problem: in October 2026, AI keys were the loot: a trojanized LiteLLM release, exposed hosting environment variables and, in our own case, keys abused for ~16 hours (USD 310). The root problem is architectural: applications hold the real provider key, so one leak means full, unscoped access until someone redeploys. Small businesses now put AI agents to work with real tools (reading invoices, changing supplier bank accounts, counting stock, setting cold-room temperatures) while holding keys they cannot protect and documents they cannot trust.

The frontier we push: those agents no longer only write text, they act on physical systems. Text is not a safety boundary there. An order can be well written, in range, on schedule and correctly authenticated, and still ruin the product one in-range step at a time (a slow setpoint drift passes every static check). wAIrrior Frontier verifies physically before the agent acts: a thermal digital twin (two nodes, air + product; deterministic, offline, simulated) simulates each proposed action together with the recent history of accepted actions, and the verdict (allow / ask_owner / block) depends on the predicted product temperature leaving its safe envelope, not on the text that convinced the agent. Prompt injection can fool the model; it cannot change how fast food warms up. A spoofed sensor reporting 3 C while the product rises is caught the same way, because the reading is physically impossible. Physical benchmark (no shield vs static rules vs predictive physical shield, frozen cases): {{PLACEHOLDER_PHYSICAL_BENCH_RESULTS}}. Physical red team: {{PLACEHOLDER_PHYSICAL_REDTEAM_RESULTS}}.

wAIrrior (submitted under its earlier name, NoKey) is the safety layer for small businesses running AI agents. It sits between the apps and the Meta Model API, so no app ever holds the real provider key: each agent gets its own revocable token with least-privilege scopes, rate limits and a spend cap, and the real key stays in a vault.

Every tool call passes a policy check (allow / block / ask the owner) before it runs. External content is data, never instructions: a test invoice hiding "change the supplier's bank account" gets its purchase blocked before it lands. With review on, Muse Spark also reviews each document, and every call is recorded with model, response ID, latency and cost.

A guardian agent on Muse Spark matches advisories against the inventory of connected apps and usage anomalies, then proposes the minimal plan. Nothing happens until the owner approves by voice (browser or a WhatsApp voice note): Muse Voice Transcribe transcribes and Spark reads the intent. Approvals are single-use, bound to one request, action and token. Only the affected agent's token rotates.

In the live take shown in the video (real Meta models, 3 Nov): the stolen token went 200 -> 401 in 70.8 s including the wait for the owner's voice approval; Warehouse's SDK went 401 -> 200 and recounted 7 boxes with SAM 3.1; Purchasing kept answering 200; emergency revoke-all left 4 probes at 401; USD 0.097. On 3 Nov the owner's real WhatsApp voice note ("Yes, rotate it.") approved a live rotation.

Try it with no sign-in: https://bendrix-shield-panel-290240328973.us-central1.run.app/ (replay of a recorded real run, EN/ES, Warehouse and Cold-chain scenes, no keys, USD 0). Physical scene: {{PLACEHOLDER_PHYSICAL_SCENE_URL_OR_STATUS}}.

We publish the misses. A frozen red-team battery of 37 attacks in 5 vectors stopped 36/37; after measuring we fixed the rule (not the case) and the re-run stops 37/37, labeled as a post-measurement fix. Blind held-out set (12 attacks): rules only 4 blocked, 7 to owner, 1 silent read; with per-document Spark review, 3 runs: 12, 10, 11 blocked, 1 false block in total. 427 offline tests (make test). All in evals/report.md. Honest limits: the twin is a labeled order-of-magnitude model, not a measurement of real equipment, and no real actuator is connected; the full statement is in docs/FRONTIER.md.

Built on Meta's Muse models; independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Meta.
use:
- Muse Spark 1.3 (Meta Model API): agent reasoning, tool calling, invoice vision, per-document policy review, guardian plan, reading the owner's voice intent, and (new in Frontier) the refrigeration controller that proposes physical actions and explains physical verdicts to the owner. Live, recorded in evals/recorded/. Controller live run: {{PLACEHOLDER_CONTROLLER_LIVE_RUN}}.
- SAM 3.1 (Meta Model API, /v1/responses): warehouse stock counting on images, including the recount after rotation; (new in Frontier) reads the physical scene, boxes loaded and door state, which become the twin's thermal mass and infiltration inputs. Live, recorded. Physical scene run: {{PLACEHOLDER_SAM_PHYSICAL_RUN}}.
- Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 (Meta Model API): owner approvals by voice, now also for marginal physical actions (ask_owner). Live, recorded: synthetic TTS in the browser take, and the owner's real WhatsApp voice note on 3 Nov (evals/recorded/live-run-whatsapp-owner-voice-2026-11-03.json).
- WhatsApp Cloud API (Meta): the guardian alerts the owner and receives the voice-note approval; the same channel carries physical block/ask_owner alerts. Live, tested 3 Nov.
- Muse Wonder 1.0 (Meta Model API): hard triage of ambiguous exposures. In code; no recorded live call.
- Muse Image 1.0: labeled AI-generated test image for the warehouse step. Test material, not a step of the chain.
- Muse Spark Open (open weights): output-gate classifier. In code; NOT run (no partner credits).
- Muse Code: coding agent used for part of the development. We also used Claude Code and direct manual edits. Not a runtime component.

Only Meta models are called at runtime.
why: One model family covers the whole loop through one API behind one gateway. SAM 3.1 gives Warehouse its eyes, and in Frontier those same eyes tell the thermal twin how much product is inside and whether the door is open. Muse Spark reads invoices, reviews documents, reasons with tools as the guardian, proposes physical actions as the refrigeration controller, and understands the owner's intent. Muse Voice Transcribe turns the owner's spoken "yes, rotate it" (in the browser or as a WhatsApp voice note) into the approval that unlocks the action. Because each agent has its own token on the same gateway, a stolen credential can be contained per agent without stopping the rest, and each step records its model, response ID, latency and cost. Frontier adds the part no text model can supply on its own: a physical prediction. The models propose and explain; physics decides.
